problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$-3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+12x-12y=12?$

feedback.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$-{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-10x+4y=31?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-10x+4y & =31 \\ 2{y}^{2}+4y-{x}^{2}-10x & =31 \\ 2[{y}^{2}+2y]-[{x}^{2}+10x] & =31 \\ 2[(y+1)^{2}-1]-[(x+5)^{2}-25] & =31 \\ 2(y+1)^{2}-2-(x+5)^{2}+25 & =31 \\ 2(y+1)^{2}-(x+5)^{2} & =31+2-25 \\ 2(y+1)^{2}-(x+5)^{2} & =8 \\ \frac{(y+1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x+5)^{2}}{8} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{(x-(-5))^{2}}{(\sqrt{8})^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(-5,-1).$
